synopsis: Across the chapters, the braking system is required to work across more than 10 operating scenarios per machine; Chapter 7 also specifies more than 100 job-site types [f284, f1176, f2032, f3675, f4393, f5130, f5860, f6622, f7509, f8254, f10384]. Scenario-based testing is the validation backbone, with parameterised families at functional, logical and concrete levels and probability distributions feeding sampling, search and estimation [f315, f6640]. Coverage must distinguish forward, reverse, start-from-rest, turning and swing: four of 13 fatal US haul-truck collisions in January 2005–June 2021 began as trucks started moving with victims within 50 ft (15 m), while parking, workshops and maintenance also need separate scenarios [f2991, f2996, f3369]. Off-road collision kinematics differ from road tests, and realistic scenarios need multiple actors, machine-specific blind areas and explicit sensor-degradation conditions rather than generic proximity or weather representations [f2567, f4358, f11551, f9371]. Simulation volume alone does not establish safety: encounters rather than frames are the analysis unit, success percentages require a defined scenario population and selection mechanism, and even a validated simulator can miss important hazards; the roadmap therefore calls for hazard-to-scenario traceability and a coverage rationale [f130, f5425, f6933, f8211, f9730]. Scenario definitions are among the deliverables considered achievable before mid-2027, but field sample sizes remain claim-dependent, and acceptance thresholds should be measured by scenario [f4973, f5782, f10967].
